title: Regulatory vs Economic Capital and Capital Adequacy

maps.tested: Reported as a named GARP-book reading to prioritise, and paired with unexpected loss in exam recalls.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'capital structure in banks'; 'unexpected loss, regulatory capital, economic capital.' The distinction, regulatory capital is a formula-driven minimum and economic capital is the institution's own UL-based estimate, is the discrimination. Risk-weighted assets and the capital adequacy ratio (LO 23.c) are the computational partner.

vardeezReading: CR-4: Very Important. "Important Reading: unexpected Loss Calculations as well as risk contributions can show up." CR-5: Very Important; "LO 23.d is Imp, LO 23.e & LO 23.f: Imp (LO 23.g for RAROC is imp, but Raroc is more imp in Ops risk)". ORR-18: Very Important, with no note.

selectors.name: Regulatory versus economic capital
selectors.what: Tells regulatory capital (a formula-driven, industrywide minimum set by regulators) from economic capital (the bank's own estimate of the capital needed for solvency at a confidence level tied to its target rating), and which description fits which.

selectors.name: Unexpected loss into economic capital
selectors.what: Economic capital from unexpected loss: EC_p = UL_p x CM for the portfolio and EC_i = ULC_i x CM for one loan, with CM taken from the confidence level (about 7.0 to 7.5 at 99.97%). A red-herring EC input can be planted.
selectors.theory: EC is the distance from expected loss to the loss at the chosen confidence level, so EL is not part of it; a higher target rating means a higher confidence level, a higher CM and more EC; a loan's capital follows its contribution to portfolio risk, not its standalone UL.

selectors.name: Risk-weighted assets and capital adequacy ratio
selectors.what: RWA as the sum of w_j x Exposure_j under the standardized approach, plus K x 12.5 x EAD for an IRB book; then CAR = (Tier 1 + Tier 2) / RWA compared with the minimum (8% under Basel II, 10.5% under Basel III).
selectors.theory: Why K x 12.5 x EAD is RWA and K x EAD is only capital (12.5 = 1/8%); the CAR uses total capital over risk-weighted, not unweighted, assets; IRB takes PD from internal ratings and LGD from supervisors (foundation) or the bank (advanced).

notSelected: CR-4 a beyond the regulatory-versus-economic and EC-derivation points, CR-4 b (the three factors PD, EA and LR), CR-4 c (expected loss), CR-4 d (the UL calculation itself, drilled in topic A1), CR-4 h (modelling the loss distribution), CR-4 i (challenges of quantifying credit risk), CR-5 a (CAMEL) and CR-5 b (elements of credit risk modelling) carry no D3 shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer of their own.
